description: The text follows the standardized IMRAD (Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion) logical flow typical of scientific publishing, often with explicit or implicit transitions between these sections.
explanation: Prevalence: Observed in 100% of the samples, regardless of whether they are case reports or study analyses. Distinctiveness: This domain-specific structure represents the logical backbone of scientific rhetoric in the 'article' column. Maintaining this distinct flow is critical to ensure synthetic articles remain coherent and logical source documents for summarization.

feature: Densely Interspersed Quantitative and Clinical Measurements
description: Frequent and dense inclusion of precise numeric data, standardized units of measure (e.g., mg/dl, mm, fl, kg, m, Hz, dynes/cm), time periods, and age indicators.
explanation: Prevalence: Highly prevalent across >90% of samples (e.g., specific patient vitals in clinical cases, lab values, equipment settings in methods). Distinctiveness: Biomedical literature is inherently data-driven. Replicating the high density and appropriate context of these numerical entities within the 'article' text is essential for data fidelity in this domain.

feature: Heavy Use of Domain-Specific Abbreviations and Acronyms
description: The articles extensively use specialized medical and scientific acronyms, often introducing them in parentheses following the full term (e.g., GHD, IDA, GCSE, DoACs, HUVECs).
explanation: Prevalence: Found in 100% of the sampled 'article' texts. Distinctiveness: High compression of technical information via acronyms is a distinctive feature of professional scientific communication. Synthetic generation must maintain a realistic distribution of these short-form tokens.

description: Text is interspersed with standard bibliographic reference markers, usually as numeric bracketed indices (e.g., [4, 5], [10, 11]) or author-year formats, particularly in Introduction and Discussion sections.
explanation: Prevalence: Present in all review-style articles and most case reports in the sample (>80%). Distinctiveness: Citations distinguish scientific literature from standard news or prose. Accurate synthesis requires modeling the placement of these markers to maintain the authentic look and feel of academic papers.

description: Sentences are complex and dense with technical jargon, particularly referring to specific genes, chemical compounds, biological processes, and medical diagnostic terms (e.g., 'fibroblast growth factor receptor 2', 'paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria').
explanation: Prevalence: 100% of samples. Distinctiveness: This feature constitutes the specialized vocabulary of the PubMed domain defined in the schema. Fidelity requires not just random jargon, but the correct syntactic and semantic relationships between these complex biomedical entities within the 'article' text.
